articles.title: Persistent's Nagarro deal faces near-term doubts, but long-term story stays strong: Piyush Pandey
articles.content: Persistent Systems' acquisition of Nagarro triggered an 11% stock drop, with investors worried about integration and margins. However, market expert Piyush Pandey believes this is an overreaction. The deal offers significant long-term strategic benefits, including expanded vertical access and a stronger European presence, positioning Persistent for larger global deals. While short-term challenges exist, margin recovery and future growth are seen as achievable.

articles.title: Nifty IT hits fresh 52-week low as Infosys, TCS, Wipro & others tumble up to 3%. What's spooking investors?
articles.content: The Nifty IT index fell more than 2% to a fresh 52-week low on Tuesday as persistent inflation concerns and uncertainty over the US Federal Reserve's interest rate trajectory weighed on sentiment. Infosys, TCS, Wipro and other IT stocks declined up to 3%, with investors awaiting the sector's Q1 earnings season.

articles.title: PFC-REC merger: Which stock should you buy before the mega demerger creates Rs 11 lakh cr power financing giant
articles.content: Power Finance Corporation (PFC) and REC's boards have approved a merger, creating India's largest power financing institution with a Rs 11 lakh crore loan book. Analysts suggest the merger offers strategic advantages and improved capital allocation, positioning the new giant for significant growth.

articles.title: Global Market: PBOC keeps new overnight repo rate at 1.25%, pumps in 600 billion yuan
articles.content: China's central bank significantly boosted liquidity, injecting 600 billion yuan via overnight reverse repos, doubling Monday's debut. This move aims to ease month-end funding pressures for banks. The People's Bank of China maintained the borrowing cost at 1.25%, offering a new tool for fine-tuning short-term cash needs without altering broader monetary policy. This increased support signals a focus on stable money markets and economic activity.

articles.title: US Stock Market: Rising equity financing costs cast shadow over Wall Street's rally
articles.content: US stock markets are facing a new hurdle as borrowing costs for financing equity positions surge. Record demand for leveraged investments and derivatives activity are straining bank capacity, pushing up financing expenses. This trend, particularly concentrated in tech and semiconductor stocks, raises questions about the sustainability of the current rally, even as the broader Treasury market remains stable due to regulatory changes.
